newsitem.title: CHINA: China orders inspections of 20 import commodities.
newsitem.headline: China orders inspections of 20 import commodities.

text.p: China has ordered compulsory safety and quality inspections of 20 types of imported goods, including washing machines, personal computers and video recorders, the Xinhua news agency said.
From October 1, only those goods licensed by the China Commodity Inspection Bureau (CCIB) would be approved for import, the agency said.

Goods affected by the new regulations included washing machines, vacuum cleaners, hair and skin care appliances, electric water heaters, electric ovens, microwave ovens, electric pots, irons, food processors, fluid heaters, video recorders, audio equipment, personal computers, computer monitors, printers, electric tools, low-voltage electric appliances and welding machines, it said but gave no details.
The CCIB and the State Foreign Economic and Trade Commission had issued a circular in September last year naming commodities affected by the safety and quality licensing system, it said.
Since the circular was issued, the CCIB has received more than 800 applications for licences from over 180 foreign manufacturers and had issued more than 500, Xinhua said.
